c6-inversion-ruling.title: CC6: the inverted assertion is the fix, not a bent check
c6-inversion-ruling.imperative: Reason on the record whether inverting assertNotEqual(0, refused.returncode) IS the fix or is a check bent to pass. Concluding bent is a BLOCK.
c6-inversion-ruling.finding: The inversion IS the fix. Two independent grounds. (a) The repo's own recorded contract already said so: ADMIRAL_SPINE.template.json -- untouched by this commit and outside this run's scope -- states the verifier 'requires a unique advance|repair|replan|stop exit' and lists decisions ['advance','repair','replan','stop']. The old assertion contradicted that; the CODE was out of line with the contract, not the test with the code. (b) The assertion is unsatisfiable alongside any correct implementation of #506: no version of 'a stop transition verifies' leaves assertNotEqual(0, rc) true. A check that cannot coexist with ANY correct implementation is a transcription of the old behavior, not a guard on a general property, so replacing it is updating the specification. Contrast with a bent check -- an orthogonal guard loosened to let a new path slip by; I verified the orthogonal guards were NOT loosened (writes shortcut -> RED; unsafe launch_id under stop still REFUSED; repair still REFUSED). Residual: the old assertion incidentally covered 'a stop must not bless a named launch', which is genuinely weaker now (stop + populated launch_id passes); nothing outside this verifier reads NEXT_WAVE.launch_id, so no launch is authorized by it today. Observation, not a blocker.

c9-mutation-leakage.title: CC9 (re-verification): cross-test leakage of the installed-bundle mutation
c9-mutation-leakage.imperative: Determine whether degrading installed-bundle code leaks past the mutation test into other tests in the class.
c9-mutation-leakage.finding: CONFIRMED LEAK, currently inert. renderer_returns_empty is the LAST entry in the mutations dict and the restore loop rewrites pristine at the START of each iteration, so nothing restores the renderer after the final iteration. Proved deterministically (repro/test_leakage_probe.py, which calls the delivered mutation test then inspects state in the same class run): LEAKED=True, and a subsequent run_role('admiral','admiral-prelaunch') in that class returns rc=1 'Admiral transition renderer returned empty Markdown'. Blast radius is bounded and currently harmless: IS_TEMP_INSTALL=True (the per-class tempfile install, torn down at tearDownClass) and REPO_RENDERER_UNTOUCHED=True -- the repo's own skills/replan/scripts/verify_replan.py is never written. Measured collection order puts only test_all_cross_skill_paths, test_commander_execute_refuses and test_explorer_confirm_refuses after it, and all three invoke the admiral mode ZERO times; verify_commander loads the replan module but calls neither verify_replan_result nor render_replan_markdown, and verify_explorer touches it not at all. So no test fails and none passes for the wrong reason TODAY. It is a latent landmine: a future test added to this class after the mutation test that exercises admiral-prelaunch would fail confusingly or -- if it asserts a refusal, as three of this class's seven runtime tests do -- pass for the wrong reason. One-line fix: restore after the loop (or in a finally), not only at the head of the next iteration.

The BLOCK at 57048457 was on close criterion 1's render leg; the remedy closes it and I re-verified by re-running my own shortcuts rather than trusting the report: render bypass now SUBFAILS on renderer_returns_empty (exit 1), G2 and audit bypasses still go red. consolidation.override_reason: The recorded fail at c9-mutation-leakage does not bar this change. It is a latent test-hygiene defect I found during re-verification, not a failure of the change under review: it produces no incorrect result today (measured -- the three tests that run after invoke the admiral mode zero times, and neither commander nor explorer verification calls the renderer), it never touches the repo or the host (the mutation is confined to the per-class tempfile install, torn down at tearDownClass, with the repo's own verify_replan.py verified byte-untouched), and every close criterion this gate turns on now passes on my own measurement. The finding is preserved as a fail and routed as triage candidate tc3 with a one-line remedy.

triage_candidates.statement: A repair transition cannot be VERIFIED at all, only refused -- the same defect class #506 fixed for stop. ADMIRAL_SPINE.template.json says the verifier handles a unique advance|repair|replan|stop exit and 'enforces repair safety', yet a repair packet exits nonzero outright. Explicitly ruled out of scope for #506; worth its own issue.

render_replan_markdown() re-runs verify_replan_result() as its first statement, and verify_admiral_prelaunch discards the rendered value (the writes come from result[...] directly). So the 'cannot render' except-branch is unreachable after the verifier's own G2 call passes on the same objects -- dead code -- and the render step is unfalsifiable by packet fixture. Out of the reviewed pair (skills/replan/scripts/verify_replan.py); worth an issue.

The renderer mutation in test_admiral_prelaunch_stop_mutation_every_surviving_requirement_still_goes_red is never restored after the final loop iteration, leaving the per-class installed replan bundle degraded for every test that runs after it. Inert today (nothing later invokes admiral-prelaunch) but a landmine for the next test added to that class. Fix: restore pristine after the loop or in a finally.
